description: Tests the behavior of NV097_SET_ALPHA_FUNC (0x0000033C).
Tests the effects of NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_ANTI_ALIASING in various scenarios.
Many of these tests were created to demonstrate specific bugs in xemu and are not of practical value in typical hardware use cases.

test_descriptions.AAOnThenOffCPUWrite: Configure the framebuffer surface with some antialiasing mode, clear, change the mode, modify the framebuffer by writing directly to VRAM, then render. Used to reproduce xemu-project/xemu#652.
test_descriptions.CPUWriteIgnoresSurfaceConfig: This test verifies that direct writes to VRAM bypass any surface configuration. It sets up a texture surface with antialiasing enabled, then writes directly to texture memory and renders the texture to the screen. It is expected that antialiasing has no effect.
test_descriptions.CompositeBlurCenter1: As CompositeCenter1, but the composite uses four vertically offset taps (-3, -1, +1, +3 texels) weighted by combiner constants (0x2A, 0x55, 0x55, 0x2A) as done by Rugby 2005's depth of field effect. The composite should be a slightly vertically blurred version of the source.
test_descriptions.CompositeBlurCenterCorner2: As CompositeCenterCorner2, but with the four tap vertical blur described in CompositeBlurCenter1. This most closely replicates Rugby 2005 (xemu-project/xemu#2388). The composite should be a slightly vertically blurred version of the source, filling the entire 256x256 target.
test_descriptions.CompositeBlurSquareOffset4: As CompositeSquareOffset4, but with the four tap vertical blur described in CompositeBlurCenter1.
test_descriptions.CompositeCenter1: Renders a 256x192 surface with NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_ANTI_ALIASING_CENTER_1, then samples it as a linear texture whose image rect matches the surface pitch to draw a full screen quad into a 256x256 swizzled surface. The left side of the screen shows the source surface, the right side shows the swizzled composite at 1:1. The composite should contain the entire source image stretched to fill the 256x256 target. This is the non-antialiased control case.
test_descriptions.CompositeCenterCorner2: As CompositeCenter1, but the source uses NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_ANTI_ALIASING_CENTER_CORNER_2, so the backing surface (and texture image rect) is 512x192. The composite should contain the entire source image (all 8 bars and the full arrow) stretched to fill the 256x256 target, just as in CompositeCenter1.
test_descriptions.CompositeSquareOffset4: As CompositeCenter1, but the source uses NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_ANTI_ALIASING_SQUARE_OFFSET_4, so the backing surface (and texture image rect) is 512x384. The composite should contain the entire source image stretched to fill the 256x256 target.

description: Tests behavior when vertex attributes are not provided but are used by shaders.

For various types of geometry, a fully specified primitive is rendered, followed by an identical (but position-transformed) primitive where only the vertex positions are provided and all other attributes bleed over from the fully specified primitive.

Each test picks a separate vertex attribute (e.g., weight, normal, ...) and sets it to a test value. The shader code will convert the attribute under test into a color.

Attributes with three parameters (iNormal) will have their alpha forced to 1.f.

Attributes with one parameter (e.g., iWeight) will be repeated into the red and green channels with their blue and alpha forced to 1.f.

test_descriptions.D3DColor-da: Renders a triangle whose diffuse color comes from a UB_D3D vertex array (green for the first two vertices, 0xFFE08020 for the last), then renders a test triangle on the right that only provides positions. The left triangle should be a green to orange gradient. The test triangle should be solid orange (the carried value retains the shader-visible BGRA order); blue indicates the raw memory byte order was carried instead.
test_descriptions.D3DColor-stride0: As D3DColor-da, but the UB_D3D diffuse array has a stride of 0 so element 0 (0xFFE08020) is used for every vertex. Both triangles should be solid orange; any green indicates the stride was not treated as 0.

test_descriptions.SquashedDrawArrays: Renders two triangles from a single vertex buffer using back-to-back BEGIN/DRAW_ARRAYS/END sequences with no other methods between them. The first draw (left) uses vertices 3-5 and ends on a red vertex, the second (middle) uses vertices 0-2 and ends on a blue vertex. A test triangle (right) that only provides positions is then rendered with its diffuse color carried over. It should be solid blue, the last vertex submitted; red indicates that the highest vertex index was carried instead.

description: Tests behavior of various float inputs to vertex shaders including NaN, INF, etc.
The test renders a number of quads. The leftmost quad passes through the raw value as
diffuse.rgb
and subsequent columns multiply each component by the value listed in the column header.
The values vary from the top to the bottom of the quad with the top and bottom values displayed above the "Multiplier" header.

test_descriptions.colors: Tests behavior of the color channels when given -NaN and NaN.

test_descriptions.1-DstAlpha_ARGB8: Demonstrates behavior of blend func ADD (1 - DstAlpha) (Zero) with surface mode NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_COLOR_LE_A8R8G8B8. The background is initialized to various colors (see labels) via a DIFFUSE quad render. A white quad is then blended on top and the final composition rendered to the backbuffer with alpha forced to 1.0 to display the effect on the color channels.

description: Tests the effects of NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION, NV097_SET_BLEND_FUNC_SFACTOR, and NV097_SET_BLEND_FUNC_DFACTOR on rendering unsigned textures.
All test names are of the form <sfactor>-<equation>-<dfactor> where:

sfactor/dfactor are one of: 0 - ZERO, 1 - ONE, srcRGB - SRC_COLOR, 1-srcRGB - ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR, srcA - SRC_ALPHA, 1-srcA - ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, dstA - DST_ALPHA, 1-dstA - ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA, dstRGB - DST_COLOR, 1-dstRGB - ONE_MINUS_DST_COLOR, srcAsat - SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE, cRGB - CONSTANT_COLOR, 1-cRGB - ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR, cA - CONSTANT_ALPHA, 1-cA - ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_ALPHA

equation is one of: ADD - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_FUNC_ADD, SUB - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_FUNC_SUBTRACT, REVSUB - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_FUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT, MIN - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_MIN, MAX - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_MAX, SADD - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_FUNC_ADD_SIGNED, SREVSUB - NV097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION_V_FUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT_SIGNED,
The left, center, and right renders are all composited against a 16 pixel checkerboard pattern alternating between a background color and fully opaque black.
On the left side of the screen, a column of squares is rendered with colors blended with the checkerboard and alpha always set to 0xDD.

In the center of the screen, a stack of concentric squares is rendered with colors that are not blended and alpha values blended with the checkerboard (the first 16x16 will be blended with the BG color, the next with full opaque black, etc...). Each square is composited with the previous square from outside to inside, so the outermost is only blended with the checkerboard, the next is blended with both the checkerboard and the result of the outermost blend, etc...
On the right side of the screen, a column of squares is rendered with both color and alpha values blended.

description: Tests the behavior of various write masks on NV097_CLEAR_SURFACE.
Color mask (C*) tests: Each test draws some geometry, then modifies the NV097_SET_COLOR_MASK, NV097_SET_DEPTH_MASK, and NV097_SET_STENCIL_MASK settings, then invokes NV097_CLEAR_SURFACE.
In all cases, the clear color is set to 0x7F7F7F7F and the depth value is set to 0xFFFFFFFF.

Surface format color (SFC*) tests: Each test clears a render target surface and then renders it as a texture with alpha blending disabled in order to test the interaction of surface format with NV097_CLEAR_SURFACE_COLOR.

description: Tests NV097_SET_COLOR_KEY_COLOR (0x0AE0) and the NV097_SET_TEXTURE_CONTROL0_COLOR_KEY_MODE color key functions.
NV097_SET_TEXTURE_CONTROL0_COLOR_KEY_MODE is used to instruct the hardware what to do when a texel's value matches a color key. See ColorKeyMode for the supported modes.
NV097_SET_COLOR_KEY_COLOR is used to instruct the hardware which texels should have the color key mode applied.
Each test renders a series of quads, with each quad being divided into four subcomponents (NW = northwest/top left, etc...):

NW: Checkerboard alternating a color-keyed color and a light grey. NE: Checkerboard alternating a dark grey and an alpha-keyed color. SW: Checkerboard alternating the color-keyed color with alpha from the alpha key and the color keyed color with 0xFF alpha that matches none of the keys. SE: Checkerboard alternating a non-keyed color with alpha from the color key and a non-keyed color with alpha from the alpha key.

test_descriptions.FixedTex_Alpha: With the fixed function pipeline, zero out just the alpha channel for all places where the colorkey matches the value of a texel. RGB channels are unaffected. This should omit all texels that match the color key.
test_descriptions.FixedTex_AlphaColor: With the fixed function pipeline, kill the texel completely for wherever the color key matches the value of a texel. This completely masks the texel rather than simply zero-ing out values. See IgnAlphaCh_FixedTex_AlphaColor. This should omit all texels that match the color key.
test_descriptions.FixedTex_Color: With the fixed function pipeline, zero out the color and alpha channels for all places where the color key matches the value of a texel. Note that the Alpha channel is also set to zero. This should omit all texels that match the color key.
test_descriptions.FixedTex_Disabled: With the fixed function pipeline, make no changes to any texel whose value matches the color key. This should render all texels as fully opaque with their original colors.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_FixedTex_Alpha: With the fixed function pipeline, set the color key mode to clear just the alpha channel for matching texels. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels, forcing pixels to be rendered opaque despite matching the color key. This should render all texels fully opaque with their original colors, since the texel alpha is ignored during texturing.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_FixedTex_AlphaColor: With the fixed function pipeline, kill the texel completely for wherever the color key matches the value of a texel. This completely masks the texel rather than simply zero-ing out values. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels. This omits killed texels even though the combiner sets them to fully opaque during texturing.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_FixedTex_Color: With the fixed function pipeline, zero out the color and alpha channels for all places where the color key matches the value of a texel. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels, forcing pixels to be rendered opaque despite matching the color key. This should render matching texels as fully black, since their RGB values were zeroed out and the zeroed alpha channel is ignored.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_FixedTex_Disabled: With the fixed function pipeline, make no changes to any texel whose value matches the color key. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels. This should render all texels as fully opaque with their original colors.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_ProgTex_Alpha: With a programmable shader, set the color key mode to clear just the alpha channel for matching texels. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels, forcing pixels to be rendered opaque despite matching the color key. This should render all texels fully opaque with their original colors, since the texel alpha is ignored during texturing.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_ProgTex_AlphaColor: With a programmable shader, kill the texel completely for wherever the color key matches the value of a texel. This completely masks the texel rather than simply zero-ing out values. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels. This omits killed texels even though the combiner sets them to fully opaque during texturing.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_ProgTex_Color: With a programmable shader, zero out the color and alpha channels for all places where the color key matches the value of a texel. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels, forcing pixels to be rendered opaque despite matching the color key. This should render matching texels as fully black, since their RGB values were zeroed out and the zeroed alpha channel is ignored.
test_descriptions.IgnAlphaCh_ProgTex_Disabled: With a programmable shader, make no changes to any texel whose value matches the color key. When rendering, set the final combiner to use an alpha value of 0xFF for all texels. This should render all texels as fully opaque with their original colors.
test_descriptions.ProgTex_Alpha: With a programmable shader, zero out just the alpha channel for all places where the colorkey matches the value of a texel. RGB channels are unaffected. This should omit all texels that match the color key.
test_descriptions.ProgTex_AlphaColor: With a programmable shader, kill the texel completely for wherever the color key matches the value of a texel. This completely masks the texel rather than simply zero-ing out values. See IgnAlphaCh_FixedTex_AlphaColor. This should omit all texels that match the color key.
test_descriptions.ProgTex_Color: With a programmable shader, zero out the color and alpha channels for all places where the color key matches the value of a texel. Note that the Alpha channel is also set to zero. This should omit all texels that match the color key.
test_descriptions.ProgTex_Disabled: With a programmable shader, make no changes to any texel whose value matches the color key. This should render all texels as fully opaque with their original colors.
test_descriptions.UnsampledTex: Demonstrates that the color keys are independent of whether the associated texture stage is used in the final composition or not. With a programable shader, draw two quads with the color key mode set to kill matching texels. In both cases, the final color combiner only samples from texture 0. The left quad renders with the blue color key as key 0. The right quad enables the second texture stage, keeps key 0, and adds the magenta color key with an alpha value forced to 0xFF as key 1. The left image should have the blue color in the NW checkerboard killed. The right image should have the blue color in the NW checkerboard killed, but also the secondary blue color in the SW checkerboard killed. This is because the unsampled magenta texture's SW secondary color matches the magenta + 0xFF alpha enabled as a color key in the second operation.
test_descriptions.XAlphaFormat: Demonstrates that the alpha component of textures using an "X" alpha mode (e.g., NV097_SET_TEXTURE_FORMAT_COLOR_LU_IMAGE_X8R8G8B8) are matched against color keys without respect to their alpha value.

description: Tests behavior when the color buffer and z/stencil buffers overlap in RAM.
WARNING: These tests are non-deterministic on Xbox hardware. The primary intent of these tests is to verify that emulators do not crash.

test_descriptions.AdjacentWithAA: Points a 64x64 A8R8G8B8 color surface at texture memory with 4x square-offset antialiasing enabled, with the Z24S8 zeta surface placed immediately after the end of the color surface (based on the non-antialiased size). A quad with diffuse 0x00A8BF00 is drawn into them with depth writes enabled and the surfaces are then restored to the framebuffer. Nothing is drawn to the framebuffer, so the capture shows only the label text on a dark gray background.
test_descriptions.AdjacentWithClipOffset_l: Points a 128x128 linear A8R8G8B8 color surface at texture memory, with the Z24S8 zeta surface placed immediately after the end of the color surface. The surfaces are cleared, the surface clip is set to (1, 1) with a size of 126x126, and a quad with diffuse 0x00A8BF00 is drawn into them with depth writes enabled. The surfaces are then restored to the framebuffer. Nothing is drawn to the framebuffer, so the capture shows only the label text on a dark gray background.
test_descriptions.AdjacentWithClipOffset_sz: Identical to AdjacentWithClipOffset_l, except that the surfaces are swizzled when the clip offset is applied. The capture shows only the label text on a dark gray background.
test_descriptions.ColorIntoZeta: Clears the framebuffer color to 0xFE242424 and zeta to 0, then sets the color context DMA to the zeta DMA object so that both targets share the zeta buffer. A quad with diffuse 0x00BFFF00 at Z=0 is drawn with depth test ALWAYS and depth writes enabled. The color DMA is restored and the color buffer is cleared again, so the color capture shows only the label text on the dark gray background. The result is non-deterministic: within the quad, the zeta capture mostly holds the drawn color (labeled ZB~=0x00BFFF00), with a speckled stair-stepped band of other values that varies between runs. The zeta buffer outside the quad remains 0.
test_descriptions.ColorMaskedZetaOntoColor: Uses a 128x128 A8R8G8B8 color surface (C) and a Z24S8 zeta surface (Z), both linear and located in texture memory. C is filled with a red backdrop with color writes, depth test (ALWAYS) and depth writes enabled. The zeta target is then moved onto C's address without modifying the color target, color writes are disabled, and a quad covering the left half of the surface is drawn with depth test ALWAYS and depth writes enabled. C is rendered to the framebuffer at 2x scale, and the CPU-read values of one pixel from the middle of the left half and one from the middle of the right half are printed below it. The left half is yellow-green and reads 0xDC87FC33: the upper 24 bits hold the written depth and the low byte (stencil in Z24S8) retains the backdrop's 0x33. The right half retains the red backdrop and reads 0xFFAA3333.
test_descriptions.ColorOntoZetaRebind: Identical to ZetaOntoColorRebind, except that the zeta target remains at Z's address throughout and the color target is moved onto Z's address directly (a single zero-area draw is issued while both targets share it). The left (near) half shows the red backdrop and the right (far) half is green.
test_descriptions.ReadOnlyZetaOntoColor: Uses the same surfaces as ColorMaskedZetaOntoColor. The left half of C is filled with 0x00000000 and the right half with 0xFFFFFFFF (the minimum and maximum Z24S8 depth values when the memory is interpreted as zeta). The zeta target is then moved onto C's address, depth writes are disabled, and a green quad covering the whole surface is drawn at a depth between near and far with depth test LESS and color writes enabled. C is rendered to the framebuffer at 2x scale, and the CPU-read values of one pixel from the middle of each half are printed below it. The depth test reads the shared memory: the left half fails the test and remains black (0x00000000) and the right half passes and is green (0xFF33FF33).
test_descriptions.Swap: Clears the framebuffer color to 0xFE242424 and zeta to 0, then swaps the color and zeta context DMA objects and draws a large quad with diffuse 0x00A8BF00 at Z=180 with depth test ALWAYS and depth writes enabled. Both DMA objects are then restored. The color capture shows a solid red quad (labeled C=0xFF2416E9) and the zeta capture holds the drawn color (labeled ZB=0x00A8BF00) within the quad and 0 elsewhere.
test_descriptions.ZetaIntoColor: Clears the framebuffer color to 0xFE242424 and zeta to 0, then sets the zeta context DMA to the color DMA object so that both targets share the color buffer. A large quad with diffuse 0xFFFF00FF at Z=192 is drawn with depth test ALWAYS and depth writes enabled. The result is non-deterministic: the quad area is mostly light magenta (labeled C~=0xFF2454FE) with speckled and striped regions of the pure magenta diffuse color that vary between runs. The zeta capture is entirely 0.
test_descriptions.ZetaOntoColorRebind: Uses a 128x128 A8R8G8B8 color surface (C) and a Z24S8 zeta surface (Z), both linear and located in texture memory. C is filled with a red backdrop at far depth, then the left half of Z is set to near depth with color writes disabled. The color target is moved to Z's address while the zeta target is moved to an unused address, then the zeta target is moved back to Z's address so that both targets share it. Each of these steps issues a zero-area draw with color writes, depth test and depth writes enabled, so the surface bindings are evaluated without any pixels being written. The color target is then moved back to C without modifying the zeta target and a green quad covering the whole surface is drawn at a depth between near and far with depth func LESS. C is rendered to the framebuffer at 2x scale. The left (near) half shows the red backdrop and the right (far) half is green.

description: Tests behavior of NV097_SET_COMBINER_* and NV097_SET_SPECULAR_* final combiner operations.

test_descriptions.AlphaFromBlue: Demonstrates behavior of the "blue to alpha" flags.
test_descriptions.ColorAlphaIndependence: Demonstrates that setting color on a combiner register does not affect alpha.
test_descriptions.Independence: Demonstrates that setting a register's value in a combiner stage does not mutate the value until after it is assigned as an output. The test performs several draws where R0 is initialized to some color then both mutated and copied into R1, demonstrating that the original value of R0 is copied into R1 before being replaced with the new value.
test_descriptions.InputMappings: Tests behavior of each CombinerMapping input modifier (UNSIGNED_IDENTITY, UNSIGNED_INVERT, EXPAND_NORMAL, EXPAND_NEGATE, HALFBIAS_NORMAL, HALFBIAS_NEGATE, SIGNED_IDENTITY, SIGNED_NEGATE) across positive (+0.70) and negative (-0.40) input registers. Output is scaled and biased (0.5 * mapping(x) + 0.5) to keep all results within [0.0, 1.0]. Each quad is split into actual (left) and expected reference (right) halves.
test_descriptions.Mux: Tests behavior of the "MUX" combiner mode, in which R0.a is used to select between the AB and CD outputs.
test_descriptions.ShiftClamping: Validates clamping behavior combined with combiner output shift and bias operations (OP_IDENTITY, OP_SHIFT_RIGHT_1, OP_BIAS, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_1, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_1_BIAS, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_2). Each rectangular quad is split in half: the left half displays the actual tested combiner result, while the right half displays the forced exact expected reference value. Demonstrates post-shift/bias clamping on sums exceeding 1.0 (internal accumulator headroom is preserved before scale/bias) and verifies positive saturation.
test_descriptions.SignedCombinerOps: Tests behavior of combiner output operations (OP_IDENTITY, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_1, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_2, OP_SHIFT_RIGHT_1, OP_BIAS) in conjunction with signed (negative) values. Verifies that negative values are properly scaled and clamped when added to a positive base value in subsequent stages.
test_descriptions.SignedToUnsignedMapping: Validates behavior when known signed (negative) values are mapped as MAP_UNSIGNED_IDENTITY versus MAP_SIGNED_IDENTITY across intermediate registers, pass-through texture coordinates, and a multi-stage pipeline. Verifies that MAP_UNSIGNED_IDENTITY properly clamps negative values to 0.0 (preserving base colors), while MAP_SIGNED_IDENTITY preserves negative values (allowing subtraction).
test_descriptions.SpecialInputs: Tests the special input registers in the final combiner.
test_descriptions.SpecularR0Sum: Validates final combiner SRC_SPEC_R0_SUM (R0 + Specular) across general combiner output operations (IDENTITY, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_1, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_2, OP_SHIFT_RIGHT_1, OP_BIAS, OP_SHIFT_LEFT_1_BIAS) with specular zeroed. Each quad is split into tested (left) and expected reference (right) halves, comparing direct SRC_R0 against SRC_SPEC_R0_SUM to isolate emulator discrepancies under bias operations.
test_descriptions.SpecularR0SumFlags: Tests behavior of specular_add_invert_r0, specular_add_invert_v1, and specular_clamp on final combiner sum (SRC_SPEC_R0_SUM). Each quad is split into tested (left) and expected reference (right) halves. Validates positive overflow clamping on sums exceeding 1.0, individual and simultaneous operand inversion (1 - R0, 1 - V1), and clamping behavior with negative/underflowing input registers.
test_descriptions.TextureDestination: Demonstrates and validates behavior when general combiner stages write to texture registers (DST_TEX0, DST_TEX1). Tests cross-stage register forwarding, in-place read-modify-write, multi-stage pipeline flow, direct Final Combiner register reads, alpha channel destination writes, and unbound texture registers as general scratch registers.
test_descriptions.UnboundTex: Demonstrates that the alpha channel for unbound textures is set to 1.0.

description: Tests behavior when modifying the NV097_PGRAPH_CTX_SWITCHx registers.

test_descriptions.GraphicsClassZero: Tests PGRAPH_CTX_SWITCH1 with the graphics class set to 0.

description: Tests atypical situations involving NV097_SET_BEGIN_END.

test_descriptions.BeginWithoutEnd: Renders a series of 3 triangles and one quad. The middle two triangles send NV097_SET_BEGIN_END with a triangle primitive, but do not send NV097_SET_BEGIN_END with NV097_SET_BEGIN_END_OP_END when completed. The final quad is treated as a triangle by the nv2a as the previous triangle primitive was never ended.
test_descriptions.EmptyBeginEnd: Renders 7 rows, each labeled with a primitive type. Each row draws a red triangle, a green quad, and a blue triangle, each in its own properly terminated NV097_SET_BEGIN_END block. Between each pair of shapes, an empty NV097_SET_BEGIN_END block using the row's primitive type is sent (BEGIN immediately followed by END with no vertices). Each row is expected to contain exactly the three solid shapes, with no missing, extra, or misshapen geometry.
test_descriptions.EndWithoutBegin: Demonstrates that a degenerate END without an associated BEGIN is silently ignored by HW. Each subtest renders a red triangle, then performs an empty BEGIN(primitive), END followed by the vertices for the primitive, followed by another END in green. Finally a standard BEGIN(primitive) - vertices - END is performed in blue. The green draw is never rendered, since hardware was never told to begin the draw.

test_descriptions.DepthFunc: Demonstrates the behavior of the various depth test functions, including undefined values (which are ignored entirely).

description: Tests the behavior of DMA on xemu's implementation of GPU-owned overlay buffers.
These tests are generally specific to emulator testing and likely should not serve as examples of how to do PGRAPH interactions, nor are they likely to illuminate unexpected behavior in HW.

test_descriptions.DMAOverlap: Sets up a render target in uninitialized data and triggers a nop (degenerate triangle) draw. Then uses the guest CPU to populate the memory within the render target. Sets the render target back to the framebuffer and renders the previous surface as a texture. The texture should not exhibit any corruption from the initial state of the texture.
test_descriptions.xemuReadFromFileIntoSurface: Sets up a render target and initializes it with a dark color. Then reads new data from a file into the render target and triggers a nop (degenerate triangle) draw. Sets the render target back to the framebuffer and renders the previous surface as a texture. The texture should be bright white, the data provided in the test file.
test_descriptions.xemuReadFromFileIntoTexture: Draws a texture, then reads new data from a file over the same location in memory and draws a second time. The rendered content should change across the draws.

description: Tests the behavior when fog is enabled but the fog coordinate is not specified by the shader.
This test reproduces behavior observed in "Blade 2"
https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu/issues/1852
Observations from HW:
A draw that cannot write anything (color, depth, and stencil all disabled) still updates the carried fog values.

Carried fog is tracked per vertex rather than as a single value. For vertices submitted inline (immediate mode SET_VERTEX, inline buffers, and inline arrays) a vertex that does not write fog inherits the fog of the vertex six positions earlier in submission order. The association continues across draws and does not depend on whether the primitives are points or triangles. This is consistent with six vertex output buffers used round robin.

For vertices fetched from memory (draw arrays and inline elements) the inherited values have no stable pattern and differ between runs, presumably depending on the timing of vertex fetch relative to shader execution.
Waiting for the pushbuffer to become idle between draws changes the association; the six vertex pattern above does not predict the results of CarryoverNopDraw, which waits between its draws.

test_descriptions.CarryoverArrayDisabledFogCoord: Fixed function EXP fog with NV097_SET_FOG_GEN_MODE_V_FOG_X (the fog coordinate is consumed directly), drawn with NV097_DRAW_ARRAYS. A control row of small immediate mode quads is drawn first: one with fog disabled to show the unfogged geometry color, one with the initializer fog coordinate and one with the shared fog coordinate. The initializer quad is drawn last so that the context fog coordinate is left at the initializer value, which is not used by any other draw. Two rows are then drawn, one per variant fog coordinate, each with three quads:
test_descriptions.CarryoverLineLoop: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverLineStrip: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverLines: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverNopDraw: For each draw mode, renders a row of three quads. The left quad is a reference drawn with the nop draw's fog coordinate (red). The middle quad is drawn normally with a fog coordinate that produces no fog (blue). The middle quad is then drawn again with the nop draw's fog coordinate while color writes, depth writes, depth test, and stencil test are all disabled, so the draw produces no visible output. Finally a quad on the right is drawn without specifying a fog coordinate. If the right quad matches the middle quad, the nop draw did not update the carried fog; if it matches the left quad, the nop draw updated it. The color/zeta limit error check is disabled around the nop draw, with waits for the pushbuffer to become idle on either side.
test_descriptions.CarryoverPoints: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverPoly: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverQuadStrip: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverQuads: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverTriFan: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverTriStrip: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverTris: Renders a series of primitives using various draw modes on the left, setting fog coordinates. Then renders a quad using the same draw mode on the right without specifying a fog coordinate at all. The fog mode is set to EXP.
test_descriptions.CarryoverVertexSlots: Probes how carried fog values are associated with vertices. Each row draws a single priming batch of points, all stacked at the leftmost position: 8 + k blue (unfogged) points followed by one red (fogged) marker point, where k is the row label. Sixteen points are then drawn in a separate batch to the right without specifying a fog coordinate, so each shows the fog value it inherited. Points are used so that every inherited value is visible without interpolation.
test_descriptions.FogCarryover: The left column triangles are rendered with the fog coordinate explicitly passed through from the vertex by the shader. The right column triangles do not specify the fog coordinate at all.

description: Tests the effects of exceptional values (e.g., inf, nan) on the vertex fog coordinate. Fog is set to bright red.
Each test renders a series of blueish quads with their fog coordinate set to interesting test values to observe the resulting behavior.

description: Tests fixed function fog generation when the eye-space position has a w component other than 1.0.

A model view matrix whose w column is not (0, 0, 0, 1) (e.g., a planar projected shadow matrix folded into the world transform) or a vertex position with w != 1 produces a homogeneous eye-space position. The screen position is unaffected since the composite matrix and perspective divide cancel the scale, but the fog distance may or may not be computed from the dehomogenized position.
Reproduces
https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu/issues/3135
(Hunter: The Reckoning - Redeemer shadows rendered in the fog color).

Each test draws a series of horizontal strips. Every strip covers the same screen area at the same eye-space depths (3.0 at the left edge to 40.0 at the right) and the composite matrix is never altered, so only the eye-space position used for fog generation differs between strips. The first strip is the w = 1 reference. Strips blend from a dark diffuse color toward a yellow fog color.
Observations from HW:

The eye-space position is divided by its w component before fog generation in planar, absolute planar, and radial modes. Uniformly scaling the model view matrix or the vertex position (including by a negative value) has no effect on fog, while altering only the eye-space w changes the fog distance to (eye.xyz / eye.w).

Eye-space w of +0 and -0 behave identically. For planar and absolute planar generation the result matches a very large negative distance (no fog in linear and exp modes, full fog in exp2). For radial generation the result matches a distance of 0 (no fog in every mode).
An eye-space position of (0, 0, 0, 0) produces no fog in every mode.
Absolute planar generation does not discard the sign of a tiny negative w (-1e-6 matches planar, not radial).

test_descriptions.MVProjective-abs_planar-exp: Exponential absolute planar fog. The model view w column is modified so eye w = 1 + a * eye_x while eye xyz are unchanged; a = 0 is the reference. The fog distance is divided by eye w, so positive a reduces fog right of the screen center (where eye_x > 0) and slightly increases it left of center; negative a does the opposite.

description: Tests the effects of NV097_SET_FOG_GEN_MODE.
Each test renders a series of blueish quads placed progressively further from the eye position. Each quad's left side is 1.0f closer to the eye than its right.
Each quad's specular alpha components are hardcoded to 0.0, 1.0, 0.75, 0.25 as viewed clockwise from the upper left.
The fog coordinate starts at 50.0 and is decremented by 0.2 for each quad rendered from upper left to lower right.

test_descriptions.FogGen_FF-exp-abs_planar: Renders a grid of blueish quads with exponential fog and absolute planar fog generation using fixed function vertex processing. Fog is derived from the absolute value of the eye space distance from the fog plane (0, 0, 2, 0); each quad blends toward the fog color accordingly.
test_descriptions.FogGen_FF-exp-fog_x: Renders a grid of blueish quads with exponential fog and fog X fog generation using fixed function vertex processing. Fog is derived from the supplied fog coordinate (the value set via NV097_SET_FOG_COORD); each quad blends toward the fog color accordingly.

test_descriptions.FogGen_FF-exp-spec_alpha: Renders a grid of blueish quads with exponential fog and specular alpha fog generation using fixed function vertex processing. Fog is derived from the vertex specular alpha (0.0, 1.0, 0.75, 0.25 clockwise from the upper left); each quad blends toward the fog color accordingly.

description: Tests the effects of NV097_SET_FOG_PARAMS.

Note that the 3rd parameter to SET_FOG_PARAMS always appears to be set to 0.0 in practice and alternative values do not appear to have any effect. Non-zero values are omitted from these tests for brevity.

description: Tests behavior when massive numbers of vertices are specified without an END call.
Tests behavior of the 2D blitting commands.

test_descriptions.BlitBeyondWidth: Demonstrates the interaction between 0x9F image blit operations and assigned GPU tiles. A blit operation is configured with a target smaller than the source. The target address is set within an active GPU tile such that the blit would extend beyond the end of the tile and a guard value is tested to prove that the blit is clipped to stay within the tile. A similar blit is performed outside of the tile, demonstrating that unprotected blits may overdraw the target region.
test_descriptions.BlitRenderBlit: Blits an image into a render surface, then performs a 3d render on top of the surface, then another blit on top of the composited two. Finally does a srccopy to blit the finished composition to the framebuffer. Demonstrates apparent incorrect ordering in various versions of xemu.
test_descriptions.DirtyOverlappedDestSurf: Performs a 3d render into the backbuffer, then a 2D srccopy that completely overwrites it. Finally performs another 3d render, demonstrating incorrect behavior in various versions of xemu.
test_descriptions.ImgBlt_BLENDAND_XRGB_B00000000: Demonstrates expected behavior of the contextual beta (class 0x12) during image blits.
test_descriptions.ImgBlt_Clip_0_0_640_480: Demonstrates expected behavior of the contextual clip rectangle (class 0x19) during image blits.
test_descriptions.OverlapFIFO: Demonstrates that image blits overlapping the pushbuffer are performed without issue on HW. A blit copying the test image over the current pushbuffer write address is queued, followed by a blit copying the data from there to the screen. This is flushed to the HW, along with a wait until the pushbuffer is fully consumed. Failure to wait demonstrates a race between the blits and subsequent instructions, generally leading to some corruption near the top of the image.

description: Verifies that using an NV097_INLINE_ARRAY draw loop that ends with a partial vertex description silently ignores any partial vertices.
See xemu#985
Tests the effects of multiple lights.
Each test renders a grid mesh in the center and renders multiple lights with low color multipliers in order to evaluate how they are accumulated into final pixel colors.
Tests the effects of NV097_SET_LIGHT_CONTROL (0x294) in conjunction with NV097_SET_SPECULAR_ENABLE.
A number of test meshes are rendered and lit with two lights:
1) A directional light coming from the left and pointing into the screen (direction is {1, 0, 1}).
2) An attenuated point light on the right at {1.5f, 1.f, -2.5f} with a max rannge of 4. and attenuation of {0.025f, 0.15f, 0.02f}.
Both lights have ambient {0.f, 0.f, 0.05f}, diffuse {0.25f, 0.f, 0.f}, specular {0.f, 0.2f, 0.4f}.
Meshes have the specular color of each vertex at {0.f, 0.4, 0.f, 0.25f}.
All colors are taken from the material (i.e., contributed by the lights). NV097_SET_MATERIAL_ALPHA is set to 0.4 and the scene ambient is a very dark grey at 0.031373.
See also: the OpenGL 2.1 specification lighting model
https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec21.pdf
Notes on use with the programmable pipeline:

While it is possible to enable lights when using a vertex shader, it appears that parts of the pipeline are not fully initialized, leading to non-deterministic color effects that change with each draw and often differ across cold boots of the hardware.

Leaving lighting enabled without enabling any lights via NV097_SET_LIGHT_ENABLE_MASK will cause all vertices to be black in color, but alpha will still come from the material when allowed by the light control and specular enable settings.
Disabling specular with lighting enabled will still disable the alpha application.
Enabling specular with lighting disabled will apply the material alpha and use the vertex shader output colors.

test_descriptions.FF_0x000000: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with SET_SPECULAR_ENABLED on. Separate specular is off, causing the green of the mesh specular to be retained. Localeye is off, using a simplified model for specular highlighting, causing artifacts for the point light on the cylinder mesh. Light control alpha is forced to opaque.
test_descriptions.FF_0x000000NoSpec: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with SET_SPECULAR_ENABLED off. Separate specular is ignored because SPECULAR_ENABLED is off, so the green of the mesh specular is not seen. Localeye is off, using a simplified model for specular highlighting, causing artifacts for the point light on the cylinder mesh. Light control alpha is ignored and the mesh is forced to opaque because SPECULAR_ENABLED is off. Visually equivalent to FF_0x000001.
test_descriptions.FF_0x000001: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with SET_SPECULAR_ENABLED on. Separate specular is on, so the green of the mesh specular is not seen. Localeye is off, using a simplified model for specular highlighting, causing artifacts for the point light on the cylinder mesh. Light control alpha is forced to opaque.
test_descriptions.FF_0x000001NoSpec: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with SET_SPECULAR_ENABLED off. Separate specular is ignored because SPECULAR_ENABLED is off, so the green of the mesh specular is not seen. Localeye is off, using a simplified model for specular highlighting, causing artifacts for the point light on the cylinder mesh. Light control alpha is ignored and the mesh is forced to opaque because SPECULAR_ENABLED is off.
test_descriptions.FF_0x010000: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with SET_SPECULAR_ENABLED on. Separate specular is off, causing the green of the mesh specular to be retained. Localeye is on, using a slower model for specular highlighting that results in more realistic behavior for the point light on the cylinder mesh. Light control alpha is forced to opaque.
test_descriptions.FF_0x010000NoSpec: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with SET_SPECULAR_ENABLED off. Separate specular is ignored because SPECULAR_ENABLED is off, so the green of the mesh specular is not seen. description: Tests behavior when lighting is enabled but a normal is not provided in the vertex data.
The observed behavior on hardware is that the last set normal is reused for the unspecified vertices.
Tests the effects of NV097_SET_LIGHT_LOCAL_RANGE (0x1024).

Each test renders a grid mesh in the center, angled such that the left side is closer to the camera than the right. Two quads are also rendered to the left and the right of the main mesh, the one on the left at a depth close to the camera and the one on the right farther away.
A light is then projected onto the geometry with a range cutoff set such that a portion of the vertices should not be lit.

test_descriptions.Directional: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with a directional (infinite) light.
test_descriptions.Point: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with a point (local) light. Attenuation is set to 0 for the light, resulting in hard edges.
test_descriptions.Spot: Tests behavior using the fixed function pipeline with a spotlight. Attenuation is set to 0 for the light, resulting in hard edges.

description: Tests the behavior of spotlight falloff and attenuation settings.
The spotlight is placed at {0, 0, -7} (the camera position) pointing directly into the screen, with a maximum range of 15.f. A plane is rendered at {0, 0, 0}, and a cylinder at ~ {1, 1, 0}.
For the "At" prefixed tests, the attenuation factor of the light is adjusted. This factor should decrease the light intensity relative to the distance between the vertex and the light.

For the "Fo" prefixed tests, the falloff factor of the light is adjusted. This factor modifies how the intensity falls off in the zone between the penumbra (the outermost illuminated region) and the umbra (the region within which the light's full intensity is applied). Note that all pixels are still modified by attenuation, which is set to a constant value.
For the "PT" prefixed tests, the phi (penumbra) and theta (umbra) angles are set to various values, including some that would be prevented by DirectX.
See
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/uwp/graphics-concepts/attenuation-and-spotlight-factor
Tests behavior when lighting is enabled and color components are requested from various sources. Also tests the behavior of non-zero NV097_SET_MATERIAL_EMISSION values.

A color legend is rendered along the left hand side: vD = vertex diffuse. vS = vertex specular. sA = scene ambient. mD = material diffuse. mS = material specular. mE = material emissive. mA = material ambient. A single directional light is used with ambient, diffuse, and specular multipliers all set to 1.0.
NV097_SET_SCENE_AMBIENT_COLOR is set to scene ambient + material emissive.

test_descriptions.BumpEnvMap: Demonstrates behavior of PS_TEXTUREMODES_BUMPENVMAP with various values for the NV097_SET_TEXTURE_SET_BUMP_ENV_MAT matrix. Values are {-1.f, 0.f, 1.f, 0.f}, {1.f, 1.f, 1.f, 1.f}, {0.f, 0.2f, 0.f, 0.75f}, {0.5f, -0.5f, 0.5f, -0.5f}, {0.3f, 0.5f, 0.7f, 1.f}, {0.f, 1.f, -1.f, 0.f}, {0.f, 0.f, 1.f, 1.f}, {0.5f, 0.8f, 0.f, 0.f},
test_descriptions.BumpEnvMapLuminance: Demonstrates behavior of PS_TEXTUREMODES_BUMPENVMAP_LUM with various values for NV097_SET_TEXTURE_SET_BUMP_ENV_SCALE and NV097_SET_TEXTURE_SET_BUMP_ENV_OFFSET. Outputs are grouped by the env bump matrix (the value of each element is identical and printed in row 1). Columns are divided up by the scale factor, whose value is printed in row 2. Rows are defined by the offset value: {0, 0.25, 0.75, 1.0}.
test_descriptions.ClipPlane: Demonstrates behavior of PS_TEXTUREMODES_CLIPPLANE. Various mock values for clipping planes are assigned to texture coordinates for stages 0 (red), 1 (green), and 2 (blue). The values of the coordinates are summarized in the image, with "1" used to indicate a positive value and "-" to indicate a negative one. The comparator function is set for each quad in the image with a similar shorthand indicating whether results < 0 are clipped ("-") or >= 0 ("0").
test_descriptions.DotST: Renders a quad using PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_ST. Texture stage 0 is set to a bump map, stage 2 to an image with diagonal lines. Texture coordinates 1 are set to a normalized vector from the eye coordinate to each vertex (technically to a virtual position rather than the actual vertex position) and coordinate 2 is set to a normalized vector from the vertex to a virtual light. See
test_descriptions.DotZW: Renders a quad using PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_ZW. Texture stage 0 is set to a bump map. Tex coords for stages 1 and 2 define a 3x2 matrix multiplied against the texture 0 sampler to determine the Z and W components of the fragment's depth (z = tex1.uvw * tex0.rgb, w = tex2.uvw * tex0.rgb, final depth = z/w). See
test_descriptions.Passthru: Demonstrates behavior of PS_TEXTUREMODES_PASSTHRU, which simply utilizes texture coordinates as colors.
test_descriptions.PassthruClamping: Validates that PS_TEXTUREMODES_PASSTHRU clamps texture coordinates to [0, 1] before passing them to the register combiners. Multi-stage color combiners apply multiplication, addition, and subtraction against known constants. Top row uses a 3-stage combiner (Mul -> Add -> Sub); bottom row uses a 2-stage combiner (Sub -> Mul + Add). Four quads per row test [0, 1], negative [-1, 0], above one [1, 2], and mixed [-0.5, 1.5] coordinates. Out-of-range regions appear as solid clamped plateaus on hardware, whereas unclamped coordinates produce gradients.
test_descriptions.StageDependentAlphaRed: Renders a quad using PS_TEXTUREMODES_DPNDNT_AR. Texture stage 0 is set to a gradient textured. The sampled alpha and red channels from this texture are used as UV coordinates into the texture at stage 2.
test_descriptions.StageDependentGreenBlue: Renders a quad using PS_TEXTUREMODES_DPNDNT_GB. Texture stage 0 is set to a gradient textured. The sampled green and blue channels from this texture are used as UV coordinates into the texture at stage 2.

description: Tests the behavior of NV097_SET_POINT_SIZE and NV097_SET_POINT_SMOOTH_ENABLE
See
https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl2.1/xhtml/glPointSize.xml
Each test renders a grid of points.
As points go from left to right: point size starts at 0 and increases by point_size_increment per point.

test_descriptions.InsideBeginEnd: Using the fixed function pipeline with point smoothing and point params disabled, tests whether NV097_SET_POINT_SIZE is honored when sent between NV097_SET_BEGIN_END(POINTS) and NV097_SET_BEGIN_END(END). Rows from top to bottom:
test_descriptions.LargestPointSize_FF: Using the fixed function pipeline: Top row renders a single point with a point size of 1 pixel (8), then a huge value with ~0x1FF set. Bottom row renders a single point with a point size of 511 (0x1FF), then a huge value with ~0x1FF set. 64 pixel ruler quads are rendered near the huge value points. Demonstrates that values larger than 0x1FF are completely ignored rather than masked.
test_descriptions.LargestPointSize_VS: Using the programmable pipeline: Top row renders a single point with a point size of 1 pixel (8), then a huge value with ~0x1FF set. Bottom row renders a single point with a point size of 511 (0x1FF), then a huge value with ~0x1FF set. 64 pixel ruler quads are rendered near the huge value points. Demonstrates that values larger than 0x1FF are completely ignored rather than masked.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_01_FF: Renders points using the fixed function pipeline with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 1 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_01_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 1 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_04_FF: Renders points using the fixed function pipeline with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 4 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_04_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 1 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_08_FF: Renders points using the fixed function pipeline with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 8 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_08_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 8 per point starting at the upper left point.

test_descriptions.PointSmoothOff_16_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing disabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 16 per point starting at the upper left point.

test_descriptions.PointSmoothOn_01_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing enabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 1 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOn_04_FF: Renders points using the fixed function pipeline with point smoothing enabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 4 per point starting at the upper left point.
test_descriptions.PointSmoothOn_04_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing enabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 1 per point starting at the upper left point.

test_descriptions.PointSmoothOn_08_VS: Renders points using a programmable shader with point smoothing enabled. Point size starts at 0 and increases by 8 per point starting at the upper left point.

test_descriptions.SmallestPointSize_FF: Using the fixed function pipeline, render points sized 0 - 1 with point params and smoothing off.
test_descriptions.SmallestPointSize_VS: Using the programmable pipeline, render points sized 0 - 1 with point params enabled and smoothing off.
test_descriptions.VSPointSize: Using the programmable pipeline, renders two rows with a point using immediate mode (SET_POINT_SIZE) followed by a DrawArrays with a configured point size (v6) parameter. Then renders another two rows with point params enabled with a constant scale factor. Demonstrates that point size is entirely governed by SET_POINT_SIZE when point params is disabled and that it is not possible for the vertex shader to influence point size. Further demonstrates that point size is entirely goverened by oPts if point params are enabled.

description: Tests behavior of points with NV097_SET_POINT_SMOOTH_ENABLE enabled.

test_descriptions.AlphaMask_FF: Tests point sprite alpha masking behavior using the fixed function pipeline matching hardware usage where diffuse RGB (black) is passed through, diffuse alpha is modulated with texture alpha on stage 3, and alpha testing (GREATER than 1) is applied with SRC_ALPHA / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA blending and point smoothing/scaling.
test_descriptions.AlphaMask_VS: Tests point sprite alpha masking behavior using a perspective vertex shader (programmable pipeline) matching hardware usage where diffuse RGB (black) is passed through, diffuse alpha is modulated with texture alpha on stage 3, and alpha testing (GREATER than 1) is applied with SRC_ALPHA / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA blending and point smoothing/scaling.
test_descriptions.AlphaTest: Basic test of POINT_SMOOTH_ENABLE true behavior. Renders a textured point, then the same point with the color combiner set to just diffuse, then the same pair again with point scaling enabled. The second row is the same rendering with alpha testing enabled.
test_descriptions.LinearTexture: Renders point sprites using a non-square (64x32) opaque linear (non-swizzled/rect) A8R8G8B8 texture on stage 3, which would normally require texel-space texture coordinates. The top row renders sprites of 16, 32, and 64 pixels with point params disabled, the second row with point params enabled (which clamps all three to 64px). The bottom row contains reference quads (not point sprites) sampling the same texture with texel-space (0-64, 0-32; "Linear") and normalized (0-1; "Normalized") texture coordinates to show which addressing mode the generated point sprite coordinates match.
test_descriptions.PolygonMode_Point: Demonstrates that setting NV097_SET_FRONT_POLYGON_MODE to NV097_SET_FRONT_POLYGON_MODE_V_POINT produces textured point sprites honoring point smoothing when rendering non-point geometry (e.g. quads/triangles) except for lines.

test_descriptions.ControlFlagsLightDisable_FF:
Demonstrates that setting NV097_SET_LIGHT_TWO_SIDE_ENABLE will cause specular and diffuse channels to be {0, 0, 0, 1} for back facing polygons even with lighting disbled.
Renders two groups of two rows of 4 quads each with the fixed function pipeline. The first row is the specular component, the second is the diffuse. Lighting is disabled.
Each quad has back specular and back diffuse colors of:
UL: {1.f, 0.f, 0.0f, 0.15f}, {0.5f, 0.f, 0.f, 1.f} UR: {1.f, 0.f, 0.0f, 0.75f}, {0.75f, 0.f, 0.f, 1.f} LR: {0.f, 1.f, 0.0f, 1.f}, {1.f, 0.f, 0.f, 1.f} LL: {0.f, 1.f, 0.0f, 0.20f}, {0.25f, 0.f, 0.f, 1.f}
Front specular is set to {0.f, 0.f, 1.f, 0.33f} and diffuse {0.0f, 1.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f}.
The upper two rows have SET_SPECULAR_ENABLE = false. The lower rows have it true. The first column has SET_LIGHT_CONTROL = SEPARATE_SPECULAR + ALPHA_FROM_MATERIAL_SPECULAR The second has SET_LIGHT_CONTROL = SEPARATE_SPECULAR The third has SET_LIGHT_CONTROL = ALPHA_FROM_MATERIAL_SPECULAR The fourth has SET_LIGHT_CONTROL = 0

description: Tests the behavior of NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC (0x00000364).

Each test renders a series of red quads unconditionally, then renders an invisible quad on top to set the value of the stencil buffer to various test values. Finally, a green quad is rendered across all test patches using the selected stencil function, causing areas that pass the function to turn green, while failing pixels remain red.

test_descriptions.Always: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_ALWAYS - the entire test region should be green.
test_descriptions.Equal: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_EQUAL - only the 0x7F patch should be green.
test_descriptions.Greater: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_GREATER - all patches less than 0x7F and the test area (stencil = 0) should be green.
test_descriptions.GreaterThanOrEqual: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_GEQUAL - the test area (stencil = 0) and all patches less than 0x7F and the 0x7F patch should be green.
test_descriptions.Less: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_LESS - all patches greater than 0x7F should be green.
test_descriptions.LessThanOrEqual: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_LEQUAL - all patches greater than 0x7F and the 0x7F patch should be green.
test_descriptions.Never: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_NEVER - all patches should be blue.
test_descriptions.NotEqual: Tests NV097_SET_STENCIL_FUNC_V_NOTEQUAL - the 0x7F patch should be blue, all other patches and the test area (stencil = 0) should be green.

description: Tests the behavior of NV097_SET_STENCIL_OP_ZPASS.

Each test renders a red quad, then enables stencil testing, renders a smaller quad into the depth/stencil buffer to update stencil values, then renders a green quad over the original red. Areas that pass the stencil test will be green, other areas will remain red.
Tests rendering to GPU surfaces (render targets) and subsequently binding the rendered surface memory as a vertex attribute array (vertex stream).
This pattern takes advantage of Xbox UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) to perform GPU-driven vertex generation or displacement mapping without hardware vertex texture fetch.

test_descriptions.DownloadByCPURead: Writes red into the first row of a linear surface with the CPU and draws the top two quads using it as the diffuse stream. Green is then rendered over the same memory, the GPU is idled, and the CPU reads a pixel from the surface (displayed at the top of the screen; expect 0xFF00FF00). The bottom two quads are then drawn from the same diffuse stream. Expect to see two red quads on top and two green quads on the bottom. Reproduces xemu #859: on xemu, the CPU read triggers a surface download that does not mark the renderer's copy of VRAM as dirty, so the bottom quads are drawn with the stale red vertex colors.
test_descriptions.DownloadByTextureRead: As DownloadByCPURead, but instead of a CPU read the rendered surface memory is sampled as a 16x2 linear A8R8G8B8 texture (only the first row is displayed) whose dimensions do not match the surface, drawn as a strip between the quad rows. Expect to see two red quads on top, a green strip in the middle, and two green quads on the bottom. Reproduces xemu #859: on xemu, the incompatible texture triggers a surface download that does not mark the renderer's copy of VRAM as dirty, so the strip is green but the bottom quads are drawn with stale red vertex colors.
test_descriptions.DynamicUpdateLoop: Sequentially renders a single color into a surface and immediately draws the corresponding quad in four successive passes within a single frame to verify surface update synchronization between draw passes. Expect to see four quads on a dark background: top-left Red, top-right Green, bottom-left Blue, bottom-right Yellow.
test_descriptions.ImageBlitOverVertexArray: Writes red into the first row of a buffer with the CPU and draws the top two quads using it as the diffuse stream. Green pixels written by the CPU into a second buffer are then copied over the first using an NV09F image blit (SRCCOPY), and the bottom two quads are drawn from the same diffuse stream. Expect to see two red quads on top and two green quads on the bottom. On xemu, the blit does not mark the renderer's copy of VRAM as dirty (the same issue as xemu #859, but not addressed by xemu PR #2800), so the bottom quads are drawn with the stale red vertex colors.
test_descriptions.LinearDiffuseArray: Renders four solid color strips (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow) into the first row of a linear A8R8G8B8 surface. The surface memory is then bound as NV2A_VERTEX_ATTR_DIFFUSE with TYPE_UB_D3D format and drawn via DRAW_ARRAYS. Expect to see four quads on a dark background: top-left Red, top-right Green, bottom-left Blue, bottom-right Yellow.
test_descriptions.MultiStream: Tests multiple simultaneous surface vertex streams. Surface A is rendered with Cyan and Black pixels and bound to NV2A_VERTEX_ATTR_DIFFUSE; Surface B is rendered with Black and Magenta pixels and bound to NV2A_VERTEX_ATTR_SPECULAR. A register combiner adds Diffuse and Specular colors. Expect to see two wide quads on a dark background: left Cyan (Cyan + Black) and right Magenta (Black + Magenta).
test_descriptions.RenderOverConsumedVertexArrayDirect: Writes red into the first row of a linear surface with the CPU and draws the top two quads using it as the diffuse stream. Green is then rendered over the same memory, the GPU is idled, and the bottom two quads are drawn from the same diffuse stream without reading the surface with the CPU or sampling it as a texture. Unlike DynamicUpdateLoop, where the memory is a render target before it is ever consumed as a vertex stream, here the render target is created over memory that was CPU-written and already consumed as a vertex stream. This is also the control for DownloadByCPURead, DownloadByTextureRead, and ImageBlitOverVertexArray, which share its setup but add a CPU read, texture sample, or blit before the second draw. Expect to see two red quads on top and two green quads on the bottom.
test_descriptions.RenderScalePattern: Renders carrier triangle vertex indices and barycentric weights across swizzled surfaces A and B. The surfaces are bound as Diffuse and Specular vertex streams with a vertex shader that blends three carrier positions via address-register palette lookups (arl a0.x / c[A0+112]) to reconstruct a 3D mesh. Expect to see a clean, contiguous 3D mesh at 1x render scale. When emulator render scale > 1.0 downsamples/filters the surface with interpolation errors across diagonal seams, shifts in index values cause address-register lookups to select incorrect palette slots, visibly tearing the mesh into spikes (reproducing the behavior in the XDK DisplacementMap sample and xemu PR #2984).
test_descriptions.SameSurfaceTwoStreams: Renders red into pixels 8..15 and blue into pixels 24..31 of the first row of a linear A8R8G8B8 surface that is otherwise black. The diffuse stream is bound at the offset of pixel 8 and the specular stream at the offset of pixel 24 of the same surface (neither at the surface base address, both within the same page). A register combiner outputs the sum of diffuse and specular, and two quads are drawn using 8 vertices. Expect to see two magenta quads (red + blue) on a dark background.
test_descriptions.SwizzledDiffuseArray: Renders four 2x2 color blocks into a swizzled A8R8G8B8 surface (paired with matching 32-bit depth buffer). Due to Morton order swizzling, the 2x2 blocks occupy contiguous 4-pixel chunks in memory. The surface is then bound as NV2A_VERTEX_ATTR_DIFFUSE. Expect to see four quads on a dark background: top-left Red, top-right Green, bottom-left Blue, bottom-right Yellow.

description: Tests behavior of NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_COLOR. Tests render two quads into a render target with the surface color format under test. The left quad consists of 4 color gradient patches (red, yellow, cyan, blue) with alpha forced to fully opaque. The second quad uses the same color gradients but has alpha set in a radial pattern such that it is 0 at the corners and fully opaque in the center.

The resultant surface is then rendered to an RGBA framebuffer twice, once at the top of the screen with the alpha channel preserved, and again at the bottom of the screen with alpha forced to fully opaque.

test_descriptions.Fmt_A8R8G8B8: Tests the A8R8G8B8 surface format. Quads appear the same as if they were rendered directly into the framebuffer.
test_descriptions.Fmt_B8: Tests the B8 surface format. Quads appear as alpha+luma ramps and are distorted and repeated due to the difference in bytes per pixel.
test_descriptions.Fmt_G8B8: Tests the G8B8 surface format. Quads set the red channel equal to the blue channel and alpha equal to the green channel. Quads are once again repeated due to the difference in bytes per pixel.
test_descriptions.Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_O1A7R8G8B8: Tests the X1A7R8G8B8_O1A7R8G8B8 surface format. Quads appear similar to A8R8G8B8, but the high bit of the alpha is set to 1, causing all quads to be less translucent.
test_descriptions.Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_Z1A7R8G8B8: Tests the X1A7R8G8B8_Z1A7R8G8B8 surface format. Quads appear similar to A8R8G8B8, but the high bit of the alpha is set to 0, causing all quads to be translucent.
test_descriptions.Fmt_X8R8G8B8_O8R8G8B8: Tests the X8R8G8B8_O8R8G8B8 surface format. Quads appear similar to A8R8G8B8, but the alpha is set to fully opaque.
test_descriptions.Fmt_X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8: Tests the X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 surface format. Quads appear similar to A8R8G8B8, but the alpha is set to fully transparent (no quads should appear in the top half of the image).

description: Tests the behavior when a texture stage consumes a texture coordinate that the vertex shader never wrote.
This test investigates behavior observed in "Driv3r"
https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu/issues/1614
The game draws with texture stage 3 in cube map mode, but its vertex shader never writes oT3.
These tests check whether an unwritten texture coordinate output keeps a stale value from previously processed vertices (as is the case for the fog coordinate, see
FogCarryoverTests
) or uses a fixed default. The behavior of a cube map lookup with a zero length direction is covered separately by TextureCubemapTests::CubemapZeroVector.

The "Stage<N>*" tests render the texture coordinate directly as a color (texture shader mode PASS_THROUGH, with the combiner outputting TEX<N>), so any carried value is visible without any texture lookup. Each row uses a different submission mode: IB (inline buffer), IE (inline elements), IA (inline array), DA (draw arrays). Quads are used except by PerVertex, which uses points so that no interpolation occurs. <N> is 3 (the Driv3r case) or 0 (to see whether oT0 behaves like oT3).
Observations from HW:

Unwritten texture coordinate outputs do not carry over. In every test, every quad and point drawn with a shader that does not write oT0 or oT3 renders black, regardless of the values written by the preceding draws. Not writing a texture coordinate from the vertex shader results in (0, 0, 0) for that coordinate.

Unwritten texture coordinate outputs do not carry over. In every test, every quad and point drawn with a shader that does not write oT0 or oT3 renders black, regardless of the values written by the preceding draws. Not writing a texture coordinate from the vertex shader results in (0, 0, 0) for that coordinate.

test_descriptions.Stage0Constant: As Stage3Constant, for oT0 using texture stage 0.
test_descriptions.Stage0PerVertex: As Stage3PerVertex, for oT0 using texture stage 0.
test_descriptions.Stage0Reprime: As Stage3Reprime, for oT0 using texture stage 0.
test_descriptions.Stage3Constant: For each draw mode, the left quad is drawn twice (so that every vertex output buffer is covered) with a shader that writes oT3 = (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) for every vertex. The right quad is then drawn with a shader that does not write oT3. Texture stage 3 is in PASS_THROUGH mode and the combiner outputs TEX3, so each quad shows its texture coordinate as a color. The right quad matches the left if oT3 carries over from the previous draw.
test_descriptions.Stage3PerVertex: For each draw mode, draws 12 points on the top row with oT3 taken from a per-vertex attribute (12 distinct colors), then 12 points in the same columns on the bottom row with a shader that does not write oT3. Each point shows its texture coordinate as a color, so the color of a bottom point identifies the primed vertex it inherited from, if any (e.g., the six vertex round robin pattern observed for fog in
test_descriptions.Stage3Reprime: For each draw mode, the left quad is drawn twice with oT3 = (1.0, 0.25, 0.0, 1.0), the middle quad twice with oT3 = (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0), then the right quad is drawn with a shader that does not write oT3. Each quad shows its texture coordinate as a color. The right quad matches the middle quad if oT3 carries over from the most recent draw.

description: Tests the behavior of various texture stage modes that require cubemap/volumetric textures but are given textures registered as 2d.
NOTE: This suite tests behavior of incorrectly configured textures. Please see
TextureCubemapTests
for examples of how these modes should actually be used.

test_descriptions.CubemapZeroVector_Bad2D: Renders screen-space quads point sampling a 2D texture in cube map mode (PS_TEXTUREMODES_CUBEMAP) with a constant texture coordinate per quad. Every texel has a unique color that encodes its position: R = x * 4 + 2, G = y * 4 + 2, B = 128. The exception is texel (0, 0), which is pure magenta. The large quads use zero length directions: (0, 0, 0, 1), (0, 0, 0, 0), and (-0, -0, -0, 1). Below them, the same texture is point sampled in PS_TEXTUREMODES_PROJECT2D mode across a 192x192 quad (3x3 pixels per texel) with texture coordinates spanning (0, 0) to (1, 1), so that texel (0, 0) is shown as the magenta block at the top left.
test_descriptions.Cubemap_Bad2D: Renders two angles of a cube utilizing a cubemap texture.
test_descriptions.DotReflectDiffuse_Bad2D: Renders two angles of a cube utilizing PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_RFLCT_DIFF pixel shading mode but passing a 2d texture instead of a cubemap for the final lookup.
test_descriptions.DotReflectSpecConst_Bad2D: Renders two angles of a cube utilizing PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_RFLCT_SPEC_CONST but passing a 2d texture instead of a cubemap for the final lookup.
test_descriptions.DotReflectSpec_Bad2D: Renders two angles of a cube utilizing PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_RFLCT_SPEC pixel shading mode but passing a 2d texture instead of a cubemap for the final lookup.
test_descriptions.DotSTR3D_Bad2D: Renders two angles of a cube utilizing PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_STR_3D pixel shading mode but passing a 2d texture instead of a cubemap for the final lookup.
test_descriptions.DotSTRCube_Bad2D: Renders two angles of a cube utilizing PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_STR_CUBE pixel shading mode but passing a 2d texture instead of a cubemap for the final lookup.

test_descriptions.Cubemap_as_2D: Renders a textured quad using a cubemap texture sampled as 2D_PROJECTIVE. The +X face is rendered as a native-sized reference image. The quad is rendered at 4x the native size of the texture.
